messages:
emily: FYI — MedSys (HIPAA customer) just sent a contract ask: they want per-tenant, per-object audit proofs that include KMS wrap/unwrap evidence, RBAC grant/revoke diffs, and signed export manifests. Need a quick gap analysis by EOW.

luis: @emily do we already persist KMS key ids and user context on export events? I recall we log 'export_requested' but not the wrapping metadata. Link: https://redwood.internal/logs/export-events

emily: right now the control-plane logs: `export_requested`, `export_completed`, tenant_id, actor_id, export_id. we DON'T emit kms_key_id or the signing hmac. also no delta for RBAC grants — only a generic `rbac_change`.

mike: short proposal: add `signer_kms_key_id`, `signature_b64`, `signature_algo`, and `event_digest` to export events. Also make RBAC events include `before`/`after` roles (redact PII). sample schema snippet:
```
{
  "event_type":"export_completed",
  "export_id":"exp_abc123",
  "tenant_id":"t-987",
  "actor":"u_42",
  "signer_kms_key_id":"projects/prod/keys/rdw-exports-1",
  "signature_b64":"BASE64...",
  "signature_algo":"HMAC-SHA256",
  "event_digest":"sha256:..."
}
```

ashley: HIPAA concern — make sure `actor` is a user_id, not an email, and any patient identifiers are redacted from logs. retention policy question: they may demand 7 years for evidence? that's extreme but legal should confirm.

legal: Heads-up — typical BAA asks are narrower. For SOC2-like customers we can offer 90-day SLA for evidence delivery. FedRAMP-style wants signed bundles and delivery within 30 days sometimes. We should avoid hard commitments in public docs. I'll draft a contract note: acceptance = signed bundle that verifies `event_digest` chain and includes KMS attestation.

emily: @legal can you propose specific acceptance criteria we can present to sales? e.g., what fields must be present, max delivery SLA options (30/90), and what counts as proof of receipt.

legal: Suggestion — required fields: event_id, timestamp, tenant_id, event_type, event_digest, signer_kms_key_id, signature_b64, signature_algo. Acceptance: signature verifies using customer's wrapped key (or Redwood KMS with signed attestation). SLA tiers: Self-serve: 90 days; Enterprise: 30 days with reserved evidence export add-on.

mike: operational impact: we'll need to emit signature at event time (cost: HMAC per event) and store signed bundle snapshots. We should also add a route to generate on-demand proof bundles (`/audit/bundles/:tenant_id?range=...`) and a background job to sign snapshots daily.

luis: infra checklist: KMS integration: key rotation metadata, key id canonicalization, and an optional `kms_key_fingerprint` field to avoid stale id confusion. Also need RBAC change diffs to be computed at write time to prevent expensive backfills.

security-bot: automated: new draft schema uploaded to https://redwood.s3/internal/audit-schemas/medsys-draft-v1.json by @mike at 2024-03-12T15:18Z :eyes:

ops: For incident/forensics — preserve immutable bundle store for 1 year by default, optional 7-year archival for billing customers. We'll need KMS access logs retained long enough to prove wrap history.

emily: action items:
- @mike: prototype signature fields + bundle generator (ETA 2w)
- @luis: infra spec for key fingerprints & backfill risk analysis (ETA 1w)
- @legal: draft contract language & SLA tiers we can present to sales (ETA 3 business days)
- @ashley: HIPAA redaction checklist and retention options (ETA 4 business days)
- @ops: storage/retention cost estimate for 1y vs 7y (ETA 1w)

mike: ack. I'll upload the PoC schema and a tiny test harness that signs a daily snapshot.

luis: I'll validate existing logs and surface the delta count — if it's >5% of ops events we'll need a migration plan.

emily: thanks all. If we can get a single-page summary + acceptance criteria by next Tue we can feed it to sales and the customer. :thumbsup:

legal: I'll circulate a draft and flag any redlines.

ashley: adding HIPAA notes inline and will ping compliance for any edge cases.

ops: will add retention pricing options to the doc.

emily: closing loop — will run a quick risk call if migration/backfill looks large.
